body.text: Which stages should a licensed physician personally plan or perform?

A licensed physician should personally conduct your in-person scalp examination, calculate safe donor extraction limits, design your hairline, administer or oversee anesthesia, and open all recipient channels. Under Turkish law, channel opening is strictly restricted to certified doctors, and international surgical societies urge physicians to perform donor harvesting as well.

When researching a doctor led hair transplant istanbul option, regulatory clarity matters. Article 9 of the [Turkish Ministry of Health Hair Transplant Units Regulation](https://turkdermatoloji.org.tr/public/media/files/Y%C3%B6netmelik.pdf) (Official Gazette, May 2023) mandates that only licensed physicians holding a Ministry hair transplant certificate, medical aesthetics certificate, or dermatology/plastic surgery specialty may open recipient channels, and any sedoanalgesia requires an anesthesiologist present. International standards go even further: the [British Association of Hair Restoration Surgery (BAHRS)](https://www.bahrs.co.uk/about-us/position-statements/) states that skin incisions for both donor excision and recipient sites should be made exclusively by a licensed doctor, while certified clinical staff handle graft sorting, hydration, and instrument preparation.

body.text: How many patients per day signals a high-volume hair mill?

If a single named doctor's clinic schedules more than two to three patients per day—or runs five or more operating rooms simultaneously—you are looking at a high-volume operation rather than a hands-on physician practice. High daily turnover forces delegation of surgical steps to technicians.

Numbers from global medical surveys confirm this divide. In the [2025 ISHRS Practice Census](https://ishrs.org/2025-practice-census-results/), member physicians averaged 15 hair restoration surgeries per month (roughly one per working day), reflecting direct surgical involvement. Meanwhile, 59% of ISHRS members reported black-market clinics operating in their cities, and an average of 10% of their repair cases stemmed from prior black-market transplants—up from 6% in 2021. Although Turkish regulations cap one supervising doctor at five procedure rooms, a physician overseeing five simultaneous surgeries cannot personally execute detailed, multi-hour surgical stages for every patient.
What questions reveal who actually opens channels and extracts grafts?

Direct, written questions that ask for the operating physician's full name, Turkish medical license number, daily patient cap, and exact hands-on role during extraction, channel opening, and implantation quickly expose technician-run clinics. Evasive answers like "our medical team works together" are a clear warning sign.

The [ISHRS Fight the FIGHT campaign](https://fightthefight.ishrs.org/who-is-actually-performing-your-hair-transplant-surgery/) emphasizes that polished websites and celebrity photos reveal nothing about who holds the surgical instruments on your procedure day. Ask every shortlisted clinic to answer these questions in writing before paying a deposit:

items: What is the full name, specialty, and Turkish Ministry of Health registration of the physician assigned to my case?
Which exact stages—anesthesia, donor extraction, channel opening, and graft placement—will that physician personally perform?
How many patients will my assigned physician treat on the same day as my procedure?
Will I have a direct consultation with the operating doctor before surgery, with time to consider the consent form?
Who handles post-operative complications after hours in Istanbul and after I return home?

faq.q: Are technicians legally allowed to open channels in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Article 9 of the [Turkish Ministry of Health Hair Transplant Units Regulation](https://turkdermatoloji.org.tr/public/media/files/Y%C3%B6netmelik.pdf) specifies that only licensed physicians with the required certification or specialty may perform channel opening.

faq.q: Can a clinic claim a famous doctor's name if they do not operate?
faq.a: Some high-volume clinics market a founder doctor who only greets patients briefly or draws the hairline. Always confirm in writing which stages that doctor personally executes.

faq.q: Why does high daily patient volume affect hair transplant quality?
faq.a: Rushing multiple cases per day increases the risk of uneven donor extraction, poor graft angulation, and excessive out-of-body graft time, which can permanently thin the donor area.

faq.q: How can I check if a clinic is authorized in Türkiye?
faq.a: Ask for the facility's Ministry of Health operating license (Sağlık Kuruluşu Ruhsatı) and hair transplant unit permit, and cross-check international health tourism authorization referenced on the [UK FCDO website](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health).

faq.q: Should I meet the operating surgeon before paying for surgery?
faq.a: Yes. Joint [BAHRS and Turkish guidelines](https://www.bahrs.co.uk/news/uk-and-turkish-medical-associations-unite-to-issue-minimum-guidelines-for-hair-transplant-surgery/) state patients should consult the operating doctor and have two weeks to review recommendations before paying.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye endorse specific partner clinics?
faq.a: No. Itinerary of Türkiye is paid strictly by clients on a flat-fee basis and has zero clinic partnerships or referral agreements.
